verdict.rationale: Obsidian exposes a plugin API (Vault interface, TypeScript) and a URI scheme for triggering actions like opening/creating notes, and stores data as plain Markdown files that can be manipulated directly outside the UI — giving an AI-native user several programmatic entry points. However, there's no evidence of a comprehensive HTTP/REST API or documented parity guarantee that every UI action (e.g. graph view, publish, sync management, canvas editing) is reachable programmatically; achieving parity requires writing a custom TypeScript plugin rather than calling a ready-made API. Missing for 10: evidence of a full external API/CLI with documented UI-action coverage, independent confirmation that plugin API achieves full UI parity, and evidence of non-developer ways to invoke all UI features.
